decisions.reason: The accepted Lit Protocol enforcement leaves the existing IPFS, Pinata, and client-removability storage rules unchanged.
Lit Protocol controls ownership verification and decryption; it does not necessarily replace PDF.js rendering, read-only behavior, or the existing reader entry points.
The source establishes gated viewing but does not remove or modify the optional offline-download behavior, which can remain available to an authorized holder.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY recording that metadata points to an ownership-gated viewer rather than directly to the PDF; no additional metadata change is required.
The source selects an ebook-access enforcement mechanism but does not request any corresponding FAQ addition or revision.
Automatic verification of current NFT ownership is compatible with book access transferring to a secondary buyer and does not alter any transfer rule.
The source does not request that the About page describe Lit Protocol, gated viewing, or ebook-access enforcement.
Ebook ownership verification does not change dashboard visibility of referral commissions.
The Lit Protocol viewer decision does not change how Transak wallets are created, accessed, or used to hold NFTs and rewards.
The ebook-access mechanism does not change referral commission amount, trigger, recipient, timing, or payout mode.
Automatic Lit ownership verification for ebook access is separate from SIWE authentication for minting, transfers, and optional dashboard access, so the existing authentication state remains valid.
The gated ebook viewer does not affect allocation of the no-referral commission to a random existing NFT holder.
